sentences.text: Mandschurosaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosaurid dinosaurs, meaning 'duck-billed' dinosaurs, named 'lizard from Manchuria' based on fossils from China and possibly Laos.
The largest known specimen measured 11.24 meters long, 6.48 meters tall, and weighed between 1.5 and 2 metric tons.
This genus holds the distinction of being the first dinosaur genus ever named from China.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a poorly preserved skeleton collected by Russian scientists in 1914 from the banks of the Amur River in China.
It was originally described as Trachodon amurense by Riabinin in 1925 before being reassigned to the new genus Mandschurosaurus in 1930.
A mounted skeleton of the holotype is displayed at the Central Geological and Prospecting Museum in St. Petersburg, though much of it is made of plaster.
Mandschurosaurus is most often classified within the family Hadrosauridae as a nomen dubium, a term for a fossil of uncertain identity.
It belongs to the subfamily Hadrosaurinae, the family Hadrosauridae, and the class Ornithischia.
